title: security: rbac-v2 - enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging enhancements
description:
This PR implements enforcement for KMS region pinning at the RBAC v2 layer and enhances audit logging for key residency. Motivation: customers in regulated industries require cryptographic keys and encrypted data to be pinned to specific cloud regions and surfaced in audit trails. Previous RBAC v2 iterations only provided advisory warnings; this change makes enforcement opt-in via policy flags and tightens audit events so operator teams can prove compliance.

What changed (high level):
- New RBAC v2 policy fields: kms_residency.required_regions, kms_residency.enforce (boolean flag), and kms_residency.allowed_key_aliases.
- Enforcement hooks in the policy evaluation path that reject resource creation/update when the KMS key region does not match the required regions and enforcement is enabled.
- Audit log enrichment: audit events now include encryption_kms_key_id, encryption_kms_key_region, policy_id, and evaluation_result for denied operations. Logs are structured but emitted as single-line JSON payloads to existing audit sink.
- Migration script to backfill existing workspace policies into the new schema and a dataplane check to identify resources that would be impacted by enforcement.
- Unit and integration tests for policy evaluation, plus an end-to-end test that runs the migration and simulates create/update flows against a mocked KMS metadata service.
- Docs: console and API docs updated to describe new fields and tradeoffs (enforced vs audit-only).

Notes on rollout:
- Default behavior is audit-only (enforce=false) to avoid breaking existing customers. Ops can enable enforcement via Linear task ENG-4122 and a phased rollout.
- Added a feature flag (ff.security.rbac_v2_kms_enforce) gated behind enterprise tier for Dedicated/Private installs.

Backwards compatibility: existing policies remain valid; the migration script adds defaults. Enforcement must be explicitly enabled.

Related: Linear ENG-4122, ENG-4189 (migration), SEC-208 (KMS requirements).
